body:
#1596 moved both s6 units to `python3 -P -m cps`. `-P` correctly removes the
unit's cwd (/config, a user-mounted volume) from sys.path, which is the hazard
the change set out to close and is covered by tests.

It does not cover the rest of the import environment. Measured locally:

    PYTHONPATH=<evil> python3 -P -c "sys.path.append(<app>); import cps"
      -> evil at sys.path index 0, app at index 6, evil wins

The old form did not lose that race. `python3 /app/calibre-web-automated/cps.py`
put the app root at sys.path[0] (and cps.py itself does sys.path.insert(0, ...)),
which precedes PYTHONPATH. Under `-m`, the application is only reachable through
the editable install's .pth, and .pth entries are appended during site
processing — after PYTHONPATH.

Also uncovered by -P: .pth files in site-packages, sitecustomize/usercustomize,
and a /config-based PYTHONUSERBASE or HOME.

Not exploitable in the shipped image: no PYTHONPATH is set anywhere in the
Dockerfile or the s6 units, and setting one requires control of the container's
environment, which is already the deployment-control boundary. Recorded because
the code comments read as though -P is comprehensive, and a future change that
starts setting PYTHONPATH would silently reopen the exact hazard -P was added
for.

Cheapest hardening if wanted: have the units export PYTHONPATH= explicitly, or
pin the absence with a test alongside the existing -P tests.

resolution.note: Shipped in #2121: both launch units run env -u PYTHONPATH PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 python3 -P -m cps; hostile-PYTHONPATH control test pins it.

title: python -m cps resolves via the editable .pth, so PYTHONPATH now outranks the application
